section_summary: This section (pages 1–67) documents the postwar reorganization and decentralization of the Japanese police system under Allied occupation between October 1947 and May 1949. It details negotiations between Japanese Prime Minister Tetsu Katayama and Supreme Commander Douglas MacArthur over the Police Law, the establishment of the National Rural Police and municipal police forces, and the creation of the Maritime Safety Board. It also covers debates within SCAP and the U.S. State Department regarding police arms shortages, coordination weaknesses, internal security threats, and the implementation of National Security Council policy (NSC 13/2).

subfiles.about: A Department of State form designating an attached copy as the official record copy for Tokyo Despatch No. 1334.
subfiles.from: Department of State Division of Communications and Records
subfiles.summary: State Department form designating an attached copy as the record copy for Tokyo Despatch 1334.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form for Despatch No. 1334

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting correspondence between Prime Minister Katayama and General MacArthur, a Cabinet statement, and press reactions concerning police reform.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards correspondence between Katayama and MacArthur on police reform, Nishio's statement, and Japanese press commentary.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 1334: Reform of Japanese Police System

subfiles.about: A letter and policy plan from Prime Minister Katayama proposing a compromise structure for reorganizing the Japanese police.
subfiles.summary: Katayama outlines the Japanese Government's plan for police reform, proposing a compromise between centralized and decentralized models. The proposal retains a 30,000-man national police while delegating local police powers to municipalities, requesting an overall police strength of 125,000 men and a coast guard.
subfiles.title: Letter from Prime Minister Tetsu Katayama to General Douglas MacArthur with Police Reform Plan

subfiles.about: A letter from General MacArthur endorsing increased police strength while directing strict decentralization, civilian commissions, and creation of an Attorney General.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur approves increasing police strength to 125,000 but rejects delaying decentralization, insisting on civilian-controlled municipal police and a national rural police. He recommends replacing the Ministry of Justice with an Attorney General and abolishing the Cabinet Legislative Bureau.
subfiles.title: Letter from General Douglas MacArthur to Prime Minister Tetsu Katayama

subfiles.about: A press statement by Cabinet Secretary Nishio announcing MacArthur's agreement on police reform principles and upcoming Diet legislation.
subfiles.summary: Nishio announces SCAP's approval of the government's police reform framework and describes plans to submit police and Attorney General legislation to the Diet.
subfiles.title: Press Statement by Chief Cabinet Secretary Suehiro Nishio

subfiles.about: A newspaper summary reviewing Japanese press reaction to police decentralization and the proposed Attorney General's Office.
subfiles.summary: Survey summarizes editorial reactions from Mainichi, Asahi, Nihon Keizai, Yomiuri, and Jiji Shimpo on police decentralization and the Attorney General.
subfiles.title: Excerpt from 'Editorial Survey' in Nippon Times

subfiles.about: A memorandum of conversation with Frank Rizzo regarding implementation problems, bureaucratic rivalries, and maritime safety under the Police Law.
subfiles.summary: Sneider records Frank Rizzo's insights into police decentralization debates between SCAP's Government Section and Public Safety Division. Rizzo discusses operational coordination, funding pressures, local Public Safety Commissions, proposed rural police increases, and provisions of the Maritime Safety Law.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation on Problems in the Japanese Police System

subfiles.about: A telegram reporting Sebald's statement to the Allied Council for Japan rebutting Soviet accusations that Japanese police constituted rearmament.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports refuting Soviet accusations in the Allied Council that Japan's reorganized police represent rearmament, inviting council members to inspect police installations.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Telegram No. 7 Regarding Soviet Charges in Allied Council for Japan

subfiles.about: A diplomatic despatch transmitting a Japanese Foreign Office monograph on police organization and assessing police armament and training.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards a Foreign Office monograph on Japan's police system, noting Japanese arguments on police strength and weapons shortages, and recommending evaluation after proper training and armament.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 59: Monograph Prepared by Japanese Government on the Police System of Japan

subfiles.about: A transmittal cover sheet identifying Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 59 as a Japanese Foreign Office monograph.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet designating the Japanese Foreign Office monograph on the police system as Enclosure 1 to Despatch No. 59.
subfiles.title: Cover Sheet for Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 59

subfiles.about: A comprehensive official monograph by the Japanese Foreign Office detailing the organization, numerical strength, equipment, maritime safety, and history of Japan's police system.
subfiles.summary: This monograph prepared by the Japanese Foreign Office reviews the reorganization of the Japanese police system following the enactment of the 1947 Police Law. It outlines the establishment of the National Rural Police, autonomous municipal police forces, public safety commissions, and the Maritime Safety Board. It argues that authorized police strength and equipment are inadequate given the absence of armed forces, rising crime rates, and impending end of occupation support, providing ten statistical appendices on police history, hours, casualties, marine offenses, and past troop mobilizations.
subfiles.title: Monograph: Police System of Japan

subfiles.about: An internal State Department memorandum analyzing Sebald's despatch on police strength as an oblique challenge to NSC 13/2.
subfiles.summary: Green warns that Sebald's despatch contradicts NSC 13/2 and suggests querying him regarding police adequacy and extremist threats.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 59 and NSC 13/2

subfiles.about: A letter from Max W. Bishop to William J. Sebald setting forth State Department views on establishing a central internal security agency and police coordination.
subfiles.summary: Bishop queries Sebald regarding his despatch, stressing the State Department's view that Japan needs an internal security investigation agency and permanent central coordination machinery before the occupation ends.
subfiles.title: Letter from Max W. Bishop to William J. Sebald on Police System and Internal Security

subfiles.about: A memorandum by Richard B. Finn reporting on pistol deliveries from the U.S., proposed small-town police referendums, and SCAP attitudes toward police centralization.
subfiles.summary: Finn reports the importation of 14,000 U.S. pistols for Japanese police and a pending bill permitting small towns to merge local police into the National Rural Police. He notes G-2 Public Safety Division opposes an FBI-style national investigative agency.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Current Developments in the Japanese Police Force

subfiles.about: A memorandum recommending transmission of a joint State-Army cable to MacArthur emphasizing implementation of NSC 13/2 police recommendations.
subfiles.summary: Bond recommends sending a cable to CINCFE urging implementation of NSC 13/2 recommendations regarding police investigation, mobility, and central coordination.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Police System and Proposed Cable to CINCFE

subfiles.about: A draft joint State-Army cable requesting information on police equipment, budget reductions, and expanding national police coordination powers under NSC 13/2.
subfiles.from: Department of State and Department of the Army
subfiles.summary: Draft cable to MacArthur requesting details on police improvement programs, budget cut impacts, and national police coordination under NSC 13/2.
subfiles.title: Draft Cable from State-Army to CINCFE Tokyo Regarding Police Reorganization
